video.title: I Built a Money-Making App in 1 Hour With AI (Bolt v2 Review)

summary: Chris Koerner tests bolt.new V2 (now integrating Claude Code) by building a PR outreach app live in about an hour with 15-20 prompts. The app stores company and campaign info, accepts a CSV of journalists, generates AI pitches via OpenAI, sends them through Resend, and tracks opens and replies. Several things broke along the way (saving data before Supabase was connected, a select-all bug, fallback templates until the OpenAI key was added, needing a Resend marketing account) and were fixed by describing errors and pasting screenshots. Bolt refused to scrape journalist emails for privacy reasons. Key takeaway: non-coders can build working internal automation tools quickly, but expect iterative debugging; the video also contains a .online domain sponsor read.

ideas.name: AI PR outreach app (journalist pitching robot)
ideas.one_liner: A vibe-coded app that stores company info, finds relevant journalists, writes personalised quirky pitch emails with AI, sends them automatically and tracks opens, clicks and replies.
ideas.business_model: Internal tool replacing a PR person / paid ads; could be sold as SaaS (not stated)
ideas.customer: Founders launching new businesses who want press coverage (Chris himself)
ideas.problem: PR and paid ads are expensive; getting the word out about new businesses
ideas.offer: Dashboard for company info and campaigns, journalist database with CSV upload, AI pitch generation, bulk sending and analytics

pricing.notes: Chris frames it as hiring a PR person for $20-40 a month; Resend marketing plan needed.

acquisition_channels.details: Built for own use; no customer acquisition discussed.

ideas.delivery: Built in about an hour with 15-20 prompts on bolt.new V2 using Claude Code, OpenAI for pitch writing, Resend for sending, Supabase/Bolt database for storage; journalist list uploaded as CSV.
unit_economics_claims: Built in about an hour with 15-20 prompts
Could save thousands of dollars on paid ads (claim)
ideas.startup_cost: Low: tool subscriptions only (not stated precisely)

acquisition.how: Journalist discovery via scraped lists; sending is automated. UK: cold emails to journalists at their work addresses are lower-risk B2B, but UK GDPR legitimate-interest assessment, opt-out and source transparency are needed; scraping personal emails is risky.

delivery.how: AI writes and sends pitches; a human should review tone and accuracy.

support.how: Replies from journalists need human handling.

uk_applicability.notes: Tooling works the same in the UK. Bulk unsolicited emails to individual journalists' personal addresses raise PECR/UK GDPR issues; corporate addresses with an opt-out are safer. Deliverability and spam reputation matter.

risks: The bot refused to scrape journalists for privacy reasons; scraped contact data raises UK GDPR issues
Spammy mass pitches can burn sender domain reputation
Vibe-coded apps break often and need repeated reprompts
Generated pitches were 'wonky' and need prompt tuning

tactics.name: Build an internal tool with a vibe-coding platform
steps: Write one plain-English prompt describing dashboard, data inputs, AI generation, sending and tracking
Ask the tool what it needs next instead of specifying integrations yourself
Add API keys as secrets (OpenAI, Resend) in the project settings
Connect a database (Supabase) before testing saves
Test with your own email addresses in a CSV before real sends
When something breaks, describe it and drag in a screenshot

quote.text: I love screenshotting stuff and just dragging it over there. It helps a lot
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Quirky personalised PR pitches
steps: Find journalists who cover your niche
Use AI to analyse what they write and match their style
Keep pitches short, simple and funny so they do not read as spam

quote.text: write personalized pitched emails for me that are kind of funny and quirky and don't sound like spam
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Without the real API key, the app silently used fallback templates rather than AI.
Transactional email accounts may not allow marketing sends; a separate marketing plan was needed.

lessons.lesson: Non-coders can tell an AI builder the goal and let it explain the integration steps.

quote.text: instead of having to know, just tell it what to do, and then it's going to tell you what to do
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Screenshots of errors help an AI coding tool fix bugs in fewer prompts.
Test outbound tools with your own addresses before contacting real people.
Earned PR can be an alternative to paid ads for launching new businesses.

quote.text: Sometimes I use paid ads, and sometimes I use PR. But does PR actually work? Can I automate PR?

lessons.lesson: Secure the right domain early when launching a business (from the sponsor read).

evidence_quality.rationale: Live build demo by the host; no revenue results and the tool was only tested on his own inboxes. Likely sponsored by Bolt.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Possible bolt.new sponsorship; explicit .online domain sponsor read with discount code.
